analysis:
The two units are head-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md, documentation only (changed range is head 11-333 per file_changes; the visible excerpt lines 458-880 are mostly historical or adjacent entries). No code, configuration or authorization logic is changed in the supplied evidence, so no concrete security regression can be cited.

Security-relevant claims the changelog makes, which later passes should check against the code and threat model:
(1) The enabled-model filter now refuses coordinator load_model/prefetch_model outside enabled_models, with a model_not_selected error (lines 575-581). This is a constraint on the TB-002 coordinator-to-provider boundary. It looks tightening, but the code was not supplied.
(2) Gemma 4 and Qwen tensor parallel prefix reuse, including the encrypted SSD tier (lines 496, 687-692). This touches T-041. Claimed scoping is the same as the pipeline, with the cache salt and HMAC-keyed names, and the records are 'balanced', not exact. The changelog does not state a TTL or account-scoping change. The new cluster SSD prefix records (lines 836, 851) should be checked for the T-041 detection_hint items (the lookup-tag derivation, no prompt-derived metadata, and salt folding) in the code diffs. Not verifiable here.
(3) Rollback (darkbloom update --rollback, lines 591-597) keeps the previous signed release and verifies hash and signature. It quarantines the rolled-back release and adds an --override-quarantine flag. It is relevant to T-043 (watchdog and rollback authority) and T-013, and the code was not supplied.
(4) Sandbox setup runs the add-on installer with --plan and applies a plan automatically under --yes only when it adds jobs (lines 713-729). It never passes --force. This is relevant to TB-013 and T-061. The installer verification was not supplied.
(5) Cluster approvals derived from releases, pair control, and the coordinator settings (lines 737-741, 793-798) are platform-owned or cluster-specific. Retained TB-011 and T-053 do not clearly cover cluster approvals. Check whether the threat model needs a cluster boundary entry; this is a documentation gap, not a regression.

No finding is raised because no changed source is visible. Deeper review of the code diffs is warranted for items (1)-(4).
